findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancellation blocks all other cancellations
findings.body: The whole cancellation loop is wrapped in a single try/catch and every SendGrid request is awaited inside the loop. If one request fails (e.g. an invalid/empty batch_id for a reminder that was marked scheduled without an actual mail, a SendGrid 400, or a transient error), execution jumps to the catch, the queued Prisma deletes in workflowRemindersToDelete are never awaited/executed, and none of the remaining reminders in remindersToCancel are cancelled. The same failing reminder is returned by findMany on every subsequent cron run, so it can permanently poison the batch and cancelled emails for other bookings continue to be sent. Each reminder should be cancelled/deleted in its own try/catch.

findings.title: Reschedule path bypasses the deferred-cancellation fix and leaks the reminder row
findings.body: For a rescheduled booking this calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true). With immediateDelete=true that function (emailReminderManager.ts lines 213-223) immediately POSTs a SendGrid 'cancel' for the batch and returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row and without setting cancelled=true. This is exactly the immediate-cancellation behaviour the PR description says stopped working once SendGrid accumulated 100 pending cancellations, so mass reschedules can still fail to cancel and the old reminder email is still sent; additionally the stale row remains scheduled=true in the DB until its scheduledDate passes. The reschedule path should use the same deferred cancelled=true mechanism as the cancel path.

findings.title: Reminder cancellations are fired without await, racing the cron scheduler
findings.body: updatedBookings.forEach(...) calls the now-async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder but discards the returned promises; the handler then only awaits attendeeDeletes/bookingReferenceDeletes/apiDeletes and returns success. The cancelled=true update (or row delete for unscheduled reminders) may therefore not have completed when the response returns, and the scheduleEmailReminders cron running concurrently can pick up a still-scheduled:false, not-yet-cancelled reminder, schedule it with SendGrid, and afterwards the late delete-by-id (referenceId read as null) removes the DB row while the newly created SendGrid batch is never recorded or cancelled, so the reminder is sent for a cancelled booking. The same un-awaited forEach pattern is used in handleNewBooking.ts line 966 and trpc bookings.tsx line 488. These promises need to be collected and awaited.

findings.title: Reminders cancelled shortly before send time can still be delivered between cron runs
findings.body: Cancellation now only takes effect when this cron next runs and finds cancelled=true with scheduledDate <= now+1h. If a booking is cancelled after the last cron run before the reminder's scheduledDate (the PR description states the cron runs every 15 minutes), SendGrid delivers the email at scheduledDate before any subsequent cron invocation can POST the cancel. The previous code cancelled the batch synchronously at booking-cancellation time; the new design reintroduces a send window for all cancellations made within one cron interval of the send time, so 'cancelled booking' reminders will still occasionally be sent. An immediate cancel is needed for reminders whose scheduledDate is before the next expected cron run.
